newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australian bonds to struggle at new highs.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australian bonds to struggle at new highs.

text.p: *Australian bond futures are likely to find it difficult to maintain the strong levels seen in after-hours trading on Friday following a softer U.S. Treasury market on Monday.
*ANZ job ads for May due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond futures are likely to find it difficult to maintain the strong levels seen in after-hours trading on Friday following a softer U.S. Treasury market on Monday.

The June 10-year bond futures touched a six month high of 92.830 in SYCOM on Friday, before closing at 92.820 and up sharply from a pit close of 92.680. Australian debt markets were closed on Monday for the Queen's Birthday holiday.
The advance reflected the solid advance in U.S. Treasuries on Friday after data showed a slowdown in job creation, and despite unemployment dropping to a near 24-year low.
The U.S. market subsequently gave up some of the rally to three-month yield lows on Monday.
Any local pullback is expected to find support at the psychological 92.750 level and then 92.670, while an extension of the SYCOM move will find resistance at 92.880, analysts said.
Strong gains were also seen at the the short-end with the June three-year bond getting close to a test of the 94.00 barrier at 93.96, up 13 basis points from Friday's pit close.
The September 90-day bill futures contract was practically discounting a 25 basis point easing in current official 5.5 percent interest rates at 94.71.

Talk of a further easing in policy has been evident since the last easing on May 23, and comments by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane last week saying that the economy still had considerable spare capacity did little to dampen such speculation.

This week will see that latest state of the labour force market with May data due on Thursday, and a prelude to the report will be seen later today wither the ANZ job adveristement series due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
